task.name: Prior-run selection reports zero candidates identically whether the knowledge index is missing, unreadable, stale, or empty, so injection can be enabled against an index that was never built and look like a working system with nothing to say
task.story_text:
## Observed

`select_prior_runs` (`task/prior_run_selector.py`) returns
`PriorRunSelection(entry_count=0)` through `_load_index_entries`, which fails
closed to an empty list for every one of these distinct states:

- `.forge/knowledge/index.yaml` does not exist
- the file exists but is unparseable YAML
- the file parses but carries a different `schema_version`
- the index is valid and simply has no entries

Nothing at run or sprint time builds or refreshes the index:
`rebuild_knowledge_index` is called only from the `forge index` CLI
(`cli/index.py`). The index is also a point-in-time snapshot — one built last
week silently excludes every summary generated since, and its admissibility
verdicts do not reflect subsequent source movement.

Both live corpora are in the dangerous state today: this repository has 17
summaries under `.forge/knowledge/summaries/` and no index file; `hdp` has 2
summaries and no index file. An operator who flips `knowledge.prior_run_context`
on in either repo gets a run that injects nothing, with the same manifest shape
a healthy system produces when no prior work is relevant. There is no moment at
which the operator learns the index was never built — every sprint completes,
every audit looks normal, and the injection feature they enabled is inert.

## Expected

Failing closed stays: a run with nothing to learn from proceeds normally, and a
missing index never aborts work.

When an enabled feature produces an empty result, the reason is observable, and
a state in which the feature is structurally unable to produce anything is
reported as that — not as the healthy no-match outcome it happens to resemble.
An empty prior-run selection caused by the selection machinery itself, whatever
the specific cause and including causes introduced later, is distinguishable in
operator-visible output from a current, readable index that genuinely held
nothing relevant, and where the operator can repair the state, the output says
what repairs it.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `d0d03c05abdc6f7cd01a7bc2ad09e75891a5a4e3` captured at `2026-08-20T06:54:34.863154+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/task/prior_run_selector.py` — `sha256:11524de39b866a934c9ffa15482f2e89cbc79a054a293783510334e414e4a33d`
- `src/theforge/task/prior_run_manifest.py` — `sha256:f19888fd40760374b65f4475df40fc5f66375dc3f7680477478cc955015501e8`
- `src/theforge/knowledge_index.py` — `sha256:a5d22f42fa75e82af4bae8905d97b173c7e90cdf3814589d507ee357592888f0`
- `src/theforge/cli/index.py` — `sha256:288ce2b8386877e5a6b69b9e900781b057a94e2ca48a4866d2f43af071086c36`
- `src/theforge/task/context_assembler.py` — `sha256:6afe94f6fb71ae8a82bb43c28cd3318b88d41213251dc99b34ef9488d8747e31`

### Observed symptom

When knowledge.prior_run_context is enabled, select_prior_runs() (and the
audit-visible manifest built from its result) reports the exact same
"entry_count=0" / "no relevant prior knowledge exists (no indexed
summaries)" outcome whether the knowledge index is missing, unparseable,
built against a stale schema_version, or genuinely current-and-empty. An
operator cannot tell "the index was never built, the feature is inert" from
"the index is healthy and had nothing relevant to offer."

### Reproduction / evidence

src/theforge/task/prior_run_selector.py:295-309 (_load_index_entries):
every failure branch — file missing/OSError, UnicodeDecodeError/YAMLError,
non-mapping YAML, wrong schema_version, non-list `entries` — returns the
same `[]`. select_prior_runs() (line 169-171) then does
`if not entries: return PriorRunSelection(entry_count=0)` with no signal of
which branch fired.

prior_run_manifest.py:_build_note (line 99-100) collapses entry_count == 0
to the single string "no relevant prior knowledge exists (no indexed
summaries)" — the operator-visible manifest note is identical for a missing
index file and a current index with zero entries.

Nothing wires rebuild_knowledge_index (knowledge_index.py:158) into any run
or sprint code path: `grep -rln rebuild_knowledge_index src/theforge` finds
only knowledge_index.py itself and cli/index.py (the `forge index` CLI
command). Live repro of the described state: this repo currently has 18
summary files under .forge/knowledge/summaries/ and no
.forge/knowledge/index.yaml file at all — exactly the "never built" state
the issue describes.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** _load_index_entries collapses all distinct failure modes (missing file, unparseable YAML, wrong schema_version, genuinely-empty) into the same [] return, and PriorRunSelection/the manifest never records which one occurred
  - Evidence: Read prior_run_selector.py:295-309 — four different except/guard branches all `return []`; PriorRunSelection has no field for cause. prior_run_manifest.py:99-100 renders one fixed string for entry_count==0 regardless of cause.
- **[ruled out]** Something else (e.g. a scheduled job, sprint-start hook) rebuilds the index automatically, so a stale/missing index is a rare edge case rather than the default state
  - Evidence: grep -rln rebuild_knowledge_index across src/theforge shows only knowledge_index.py's own definition and cli/index.py's CLI wiring — no coordinator/sprint/run code calls it. Confirmed live: this repo has 18 summaries and zero index.yaml, i.e. the index has never been built despite ongoing knowledge capture.
- **[ruled out]** The manifest note function does distinguish these cases further downstream (e.g. in context_assembler.py) even though prior_run_selector.py does not
  - Evidence: context_assembler.py only calls prior_run_manifest.build_manifest(selection, ...) and disabled_manifest(); build_manifest's note logic is exactly the _build_note function inspected above, which branches only on selection.entry_count == 0, a value that is already cause-blind by the time it leaves the selector.

### Confirmed cause

select_prior_runs()'s index-loading step (_load_index_entries in
task/prior_run_selector.py) fails closed to an empty list for every
distinct failure mode — missing index file, unparseable YAML, wrong
schema_version, and a valid-but-empty index — and PriorRunSelection carries
no field recording which case occurred. The downstream audit manifest
(prior_run_manifest.py:_build_note) therefore renders the identical
operator-visible note ("no relevant prior knowledge exists (no indexed
summaries)") for a structurally broken/never-built index and for a healthy
index that simply held nothing relevant, so an operator who enables
knowledge.prior_run_context against a repo whose index was never built (as
both this repo and hdp are today, since nothing outside `forge index`
builds or refreshes it) gets no signal that the feature is inert.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/task/prior_run_selector.py:295-309 (_load_index_entries) and
:151-171 (select_prior_runs, the `if not entries: return
PriorRunSelection(entry_count=0)` branch) — collapses distinct
index-loading outcomes into one signal.
src/theforge/task/prior_run_manifest.py:81-121 (_build_note) — renders the
collapsed entry_count==0 case as a single fixed note indistinguishable from
a genuine empty-but-healthy index.

### Fix-success criterion

With knowledge.prior_run_context enabled: (1) a repo with no
.forge/knowledge/index.yaml at all produces an audit-visible manifest note
that says the index is missing/unbuilt (and, per the issue's "where the
operator can repair the state, the output says what repairs it" clause,
points at `forge index` or equivalent); (2) a repo with an unparseable or
wrong-schema-version index.yaml produces a manifest note that says the
index is unreadable/stale-schema, distinct from case 1 and from case 3; (3)
a repo with a current, valid, schema-matching index.yaml that has zero
entries or zero relevant entries still produces the existing "no relevant
prior knowledge exists" note, unchanged. All three remain non-fatal — a run
proceeds normally in every case, only the observability differs.

### Notes

The issue's second paragraph also raises index staleness (a index built
once and never refreshed as new summaries land, or as source files move
after admissibility verdicts were computed) as part of the same
"structurally unable to produce anything, but looks healthy" family. I did
not chase a specific reproducible staleness scenario beyond confirming (a)
rebuild_knowledge_index is CLI-only/never automatic, so any index that
exists is necessarily a snapshot, and (b) the selector has no mechanism to
detect or report staleness relative to current summaries on disk. Whether
the fix should also compare index entry count/mtime against
.forge/knowledge/summaries/ contents, or whether that's out of scope versus
the four _load_index_entries branches, is a design decision I'm leaving to
the fix flow rather than prescribing here.

handoff.summary: Added explicit prior-run knowledge index health reporting to the selector/manifest path. The selector now returns an `index_state` alongside empty selections so missing, unreadable, and stale-schema index failures remain fail-closed but no longer masquerade as a healthy empty index; the manifest note branches on that state and points operators at `forge index` where repair is possible. Tests were updated to cover selector state, manifest note variants, and the context-assembler seam.

findings.description: An index file that parses, carries the supported schema_version, and has an entries list whose items are all non-mapping values yields an empty selection reported as index_state ready, so the manifest note reads 'no relevant prior knowledge exists (no indexed summaries)' for a structurally malformed index — verified by writing an index with entries containing a bare string and observing that exact note.

The operator guide still describes the prior_run_context manifest note as distinguishing only 'no relevant prior knowledge exists' from 'prior knowledge existed but was withheld', with no mention of the new missing, unreadable, and stale-schema index notes or of the fact that the index is only ever built by running forge index.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
